The reason given was real: an installed tree has no <t1/>, so the shell tool could not read the manifest at run time. It could read a <t2>projection</t2> of it, though, and a projection is how this repository states every other derived fact. Version 2 of this rule is that: the version is authored in one place, and the shell tool reads a generated file its own distribution carries (ADR 0085).
cs: Verze měla stejný tvar o úroveň níž. Uvedený důvod byl skutečný: nainstalovaný strom nemá <t1/>, takže shellový nástroj nemohl za běhu číst manifest. Mohl však číst jeho <t2>projekci</t2> a projekce je způsob, jakým tento repozitář uvádí každý jiný odvozený fakt. en: A test that fails under instrumentation is BLOCKED too: cargo-llvm-cov writes no export for a suite that failed. The gate then prints what the test harness reported, the <t1/> section of every failing binary with each failing test's name and panic, so the job log names the test rather than only its binary. A binary killed by a signal writes no such section and no <t2/> line, so its unfinished <t3/> block is printed too: its header, how many tests completed and its last lines. It cannot name the test that was running, because the parallel harness writes a test's line only when that test completes; cargo's stderr names the binary and the signal. A green run prints none of the harness's output. <t4/> holds that behaviour.
cs: Test, který selže pod instrumentací, je také BLOCKED: cargo-llvm-cov nezapíše žádný export pro sadu, která selhala. Kontrola pak vypíše, co hlásil testovací harness, sekci <t1/> každé selhávající binárky s názvem a panikou každého selhávajícího testu, takže log úlohy jmenuje test, ne jen jeho binárku. Treating a passing run as valid until something anywhere changes is the badge whose derivation cannot be inspected; declaring every result stale the instant anything anywhere changes is sound and useless, since on a repository that lands to master every few minutes no claim would ever be proven except in the seconds after a full run. So the model says which of the two it found, and says it in the same words on every surface. en: The Cockpit is a faithful projection of a registry that has almost nothing development-shaped in it. Re-measured on today's master, the registry declares exactly three capabilities of kind `command` — executions.start, executions.cancel, peers.announce — and the OpenAPI document the server serves has exactly those three non-GET operations to match. Every command of the development lifecycle lives in a second program, bin/majordomus, and every one of its nodes in the command graph is withheld from every machine surface. So no development surface can be built by adding pages: there is nothing behind the pages to call, and `majordomus_plan_done` answers `unknown tool` because there is no capability for a plan transition. docs/COCKPIT_IDE_AUDIT.md is the evidence; ADR 0040 is the decision it argues for. Until this milestone existed, none of it was in the plan at all: a keyword search of the issues and milestones for palette, diff view, CI status and syntax highlighting returned nothing, so the work could not be scheduled, blocked or reported.
cs: Cockpit je věrná projekce registru, který v sobě nemá téměř nic vývojového. Znovu změřeno na dnešním masteru, registr deklaruje přesně tři schopnosti druhu `command` — executions.start, executions.cancel, peers.announce — a dokument OpenAPI, který server servíruje, má přesně těchto tři operace jiné než GET. Každý příkaz vývojového životního cyklu žije ve druhém programu, bin/majordomus, a každý jeho uzel v grafu příkazů je zadržen před každým strojovým povrchem. Žádný vývojový povrch tedy nelze postavit přidáním stránek: za stránkami není nic, co by se dalo volat, a `majordomus_plan_done` odpovídá `unknown tool`, protože pro přechod plánu neexistuje schopnost. docs/COCKPIT_IDE_AUDIT.md je důkaz; ADR 0040 je rozhodnutí, které obhajuje. Dokud tento milník neexistoval, nic z toho nebylo v plánu: klíčové hledání v úkolech a milnících pro paletu, diff view, stav CI a zvýraznění syntaxe nevrátilo nic, takže práci nebylo možné naplánovat, blokovat ani o ní reportovat.
